---
title: "toOrdinalDate()"
subtitle: "Convert dates to long, ordinal calendar dates"
toc: true
---

## Usage

``` R
toOrdinalDate(date = NULL, language = "English")
```

## Arguments

`date`{#date}

:   `NULL` (the default, today's date from `Sys.Date()`), a `Date` or `POSIXt` vector, or a character vector of dates such as `"2017-10-09"` or `"2017-10-9"`. Missing values return `NA`.

`language`{#language}

:   A single string. Only `"English"` is implemented.

## Value

A character vector with one element per date; one element for `date = NULL`.

## Description

Converts calendar dates to the long form with an ordinal day, for example `"October 9th, 2017"`.

## Details

Month names are always English, whatever the session locale, so the result does not change from one machine to the next. English is the only language implemented; any other `language` signals an error.

## Examples

``` R
toOrdinalDate()
toOrdinalDate("2017-10-9")
toOrdinalDate(c("2022-11-21", "2019-1-3", "1976-2-2", "1965-2-18"))
```
